issues.detail: The Hebrew genealogy is 'בֶּן הֲדַד בֶּן טַבְרִמֹּן בֶּן חֶזְיוֹן' meaning 'Ben-hadad son of Tabrimmon son of Hezion'. The Chinese renders '他伯林的兒子便哈達、赫西崙人的兒子' which reverses the genealogy: it says 'Ben-hadad son of Tabrimmon, son of Hezion' but the Chinese places '赫西崙人的兒子' (son of Hezion) after '便哈達' (Ben-hadad), making it appear that Ben-hadad is the son of Hezion, whereas the Hebrew says Ben-hadad is the son of Tabrimmon, who is the son of Hezion. This changes the family relationship.
